summary.headline: PVR INOX Q2 FY27 adjusted EBITDA rose 44% to INR 475 crores at a 22.3% margin, with PAT more than doubling to INR 273 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was described as the best-ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, driven by a record industry box office of INR 4,433 crores (up 23% YoY) and footfalls up 4% to 46.3 million. Ind AS 116 adjusted total income grew 17% to INR 2,133 crores, with operating leverage lifting EBITDA margin about 420 bps. Management turned net cash (INR 141 crores at September-end), executed a maiden INR 300 crore buyback, and adopted a capital allocation policy targeting around 30% of annual surplus cash flow returned to shareholders. Screen growth is guided to accelerate, with 90-100 openings in FY27 and a new capital-light SMART Cinema format piloted in Muzaffarpur.

segments.name: Movie exhibition
segments.commentary: Footfalls 46.3 million (+4% YoY), occupancy 30.4%. Company says it under-indexed industry growth (18% vs 23%) because content was spread across single screens in Tier 2-4 towns.

segments.name: Food and beverage
segments.commentary: F&B spend per head INR 153 (+14% YoY). Popcorn and Pepsi make up about 60% of F&B sales; management says gross margin rose from about 74% to 77-78%. About 85% of footfalls buy F&B.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Weak in H1 due to a lack of tentpole films. Management expects Q3-Q4 gains from Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War; a pay-per-eyeball digital ad platform is 8-10 months away.

segments.name: Network and expansion
segments.commentary: Network at 1,797 screens across 114 cities (India and Sri Lanka). H1 added 24 screens across 6 cinemas and exited 25 mostly loss-making screens.

guidance_outlook: Open 90-100 new screens in FY27, mostly in H2 and mainly capital-light formats.
Next year (FY28) screen openings guided to about 150-175 per year, with about 60-70 possibly SMART screens; roughly 500 screens over three years was accepted by management.
Overall FY27 capex INR 300-330 crores (H1 spend INR 132 crores); FY28 capex likely above INR 350 crores, plus or minus.
Depreciation to fall by INR 35-40 crores a year after a useful-life change for projectors and IT equipment.
Capital allocation policy: keep net debt/EBITDA within 0.5x after distributions, invest for growth, and return about 30% of annual surplus cash flow via dividends or buybacks.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 to benefit from a strong film slate; said it was 'very hopeful and optimistic' about H2 but did not give a Q3 footfall number.
Target payback of 3-4 years per unit; SMART Cinema capex 25-30% below normal screens and opex about 25% lower.
capex_capacity: Network 1,797 screens across 114 cities; 24 screens added and 25 exited in H1 FY27.

First SMART Cinema opened in Muzaffarpur, Bihar in September 2026 (capex 25-30% lower, opex about 25% lower, ATP about INR 190); two more in fit-out (Rampur, Bharatpur) and about 100 more signed for opening in the next 12-18 months.
300 cities identified for SMART Cinemas; expected two or three more SMART openings this fiscal.
Expansion mix is asset-light, FOCO and lease; for FOCO, only management fees are booked; for asset-light, full P&L is consolidated.
Around 35-40% of new screens in the last 2-3 years opened in South India.
demand_pricing: Industry box office INR 4,433 crores in Q2 (record, first quarter above INR 4,000 crores); H1 INR 7,618 crores (+22%).
English cinema INR 1,024 crores (+87%); Spider-Man: Brand New Day INR 608 crores; Odyssey INR 233 crores.
Hindi led by Hanuman Ansh (INR 351 crores) and Mirzapur: The Movie (INR 267 crores). Management argued Hindi growth is understated due to dubbed English films being reported under English.
Value offers: weekday morning shows at INR 99, Friday first shows at INR 149, front-row seats from INR 79.
South India average ticket price about 25% below the rest of India; management said higher occupancy more than offsets this.

qa_highlights.question: How are SMART Cinemas priced, what is the capex, and what is the 2-year opening plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is 25-30% lower and opex about 25% lower than normal cinemas; ATP around INR 190 at the pilot. About 100 more are signed for 12-18 months. Management said growth will not be compromised while keeping paybacks within 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Hindi incremental box office so small in H1 versus regional and English?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 FY26 had a high Hindi base; Hollywood was recovering. It added that dubbed English films (about INR 200 crores from Spider-Man) count as English, so Hindi growth is understated.

qa_highlights.question: Will screen additions accelerate after the cleanup of underperforming screens?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Past closures were of dilapidated mall screens. Management guided to 150-175 openings a year from next fiscal, with about 500 screens over three years.

qa_highlights.question: How are FOCO and asset-light revenues and costs accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset-light is fully consolidated. FOCO books only management fees, with operating costs at the franchisee. Lease screens are traditional leases.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ROU assets and lease liabilities decline despite openings?
qa_highlights.answer: About 23-24 loss-making screens closed in H1, which offset new openings. ROU assets and liabilities also decline through depreciation and repayment under Ind AS 116.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin expansion in F&B?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a high-margin mix (popcorn and Pepsi are about 60% of sales), supplier renegotiation, a 4PL logistics migration that cuts wastage, and volume growth from weekend and weekday promotions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PVR's box office growth (18%) lag the industry (23%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to content mix: Hanuman Ansh, Mirzapur and regional films did well in Tier 2-4 towns where single screens dominate.

qa_highlights.question: What are the depreciation and capex numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation falls INR 35-40 crores a year from the useful-life change. FY27 capex INR 300-330 crores; FY28 above INR 350 crores.

risks_watch: Ad revenue recovery depends on the Q3-Q4 tentpole slate (Ramayana, King, Avengers, Love & War) and the digital pay-per-eyeball platform, due in 8-10 months.
SMART format is a pilot with only about two months of data; the 150-175 screen FY28 target depends on the pipeline converting.
Lower rent-to-revenue in Q2 is tied to revenue-share terms on legacy screens (minimum guarantee or revenue share, whichever is higher); rent rose about 11% YoY in Q2.
Q2 other income includes INR 7 crores of one-off provision reversals.
Pending southern state ticket-price issues: management said no conversations are underway.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, margins and the film slate, with repeated emphasis on capital discipline and unit paybacks. Management was evasive on specifics for Q3 footfalls (no number given) and on the Hindi box office data, which it disputed.
key_quotes: This is also our best ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
Unit level economics, even if you open 200 screens a year will not be compromised.
Hindi is not struggling. Hindi has been doing well since last year.
So we are trying to build on a digital platform.

SMART Cinema format: 150-175 screens a year from FY28 (about 60-70 SMART screens), roughly 500 screens over three years

growth.why: Management reiterated 90-100 new FY27 screens (back-loaded to H2, mostly capital-light) and guided FY28 at 150-175 SMART screens, with first SMART opened in Muzaffarpur and about 100 more signed; the call gives specific screen counts and timing but no revenue growth percentage, and H2 footfall was not quantified, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose about 420 bps to 22.3% in Q2 on operating leverage, F&B gross margin moved from about 74% to 77-78%, and depreciation falls INR 35-40 crores a year; H2 tentpole films support it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 90-100 new screens guided for FY27 with the bulk in H2, from 24 added and 25 exited in H1, and about 100 SMART screens signed for opening in 12-18 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Footfalls rose 4% to 46.3 million in Q2 against industry box office up 23%, and management is 'very hopeful and optimistic' on H2 with Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War, though no Q3 footfall number was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 30.4% so capacity is not constrained, but FY28 capex is guided above INR 350 crores for 150-175 SMART screens a year and about 300 cities are identified, so a capex plan is likely to be formalised.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 EBITDA rose 56% and H1 PAT rose 233%, and management is confident on the H2 film slate, but no revenue or margin guidance was raised numerically.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Screen additions (90-100) and capex (INR 300-330 crores) are held or cut, and the ad revenue risk depends on the Q3-Q4 slate and an 8-10 month digital platform.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SMART Cinema format is piloted in Muzaffarpur at about INR 190 ATP with two more in fit-out (Rampur, Bharatpur), and the pay-per-eyeball digital ad platform is 8-10 months away.

rows.label: SMART Cinema low-price format rollout
rows.why: SMART ATP is about INR 190 against INR 298 company-wide, with capex 25-30% lower and opex about 25% lower, and about 100 more signed for opening in 12-18 months.

rows.label: Debt-free balance sheet and cash returns
rows.why: Net cash of INR 141 crores at end-September after H1 FREE cash flow of INR 604 crores, with a policy to return about 30% of surplus cash flow and keep net debt/EBITDA within 0.5x.

rows.label: Ad revenue recovery on tentpole films
rows.why: Advertising was weak in H1 due to a lack of tentpole films, and management expects Q3-Q4 gains from Ramayana, King, Avengers and Love & War, but no ad figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, F&B gross margin, the SMART format's paybacks and H2 films, and stayed evasive on Q3 footfalls and disputed the Hindi box office data. Analysts pressed on the lag versus industry growth, the SMART pilot's short data history and the 150-175 screen FY28 target.
